examples.problem_statement: Mixture A weighs 18 grams and is 50% aluminum. Mixture B weighs 32 grams and is 37.5% aluminum. The two mixtures are combined. Quantity A: the percent of the resultant combination that is not aluminum. Quantity B: 58%. (A) Quantity A is greater. (B) Quantity B is greater. (C) The two quantities are equal. (D) The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.

solution.description: Take the complement of Mixture A's aluminum percentage, because the question asks for the part that is NOT aluminum.
Multiply Mixture A's 18 gram weight by its non-aluminum fraction 0.5 to get the grams of A that are not aluminum.
Take the complement of Mixture B's aluminum percentage and rewrite it as the fraction 5/8 to make the next multiplication clean.
Multiply Mixture B's 32 gram weight by its non-aluminum fraction 5/8 to get the grams of B that are not aluminum.

solution.result: 29 grams non-aluminum out of 50 total grams
solution.description: Add the two non-aluminum amounts, and separately add the two mixture weights, to get the part and the whole of the combination.

solution.result: Quantity A = 58\%, equal to Quantity B
solution.description: Convert the part-over-whole ratio to a percent by scaling the denominator to 100, then compare it with Quantity B.

key_reminders: If a mixture is p% one component, it is (100 - p)% everything else.
Combine mixtures by summing the component amounts and summing the total weights separately; percentages themselves do not add.
A fraction over 50 becomes a percent by doubling numerator and denominator to reach /100.
common_mistakes: Averaging 50% and 37.5% (or their complements) directly instead of weighting by the 18 g and 32 g masses.
Answering with the aluminum percentage (42%) instead of the NOT-aluminum percentage the question asks for.

solution.operation: Apply the cyclicity principle to the units digits of the factors
solution.result: Only units digits matter for the units digit of a product
solution.description: Recognise that the units digit of the whole product depends solely on the units digits of the factors, so the cyclicity principle applies.

solution.operation: Units digits of 1^7, 2^7, \dots, 9^7 repeat once for every block of ten numbers
solution.result: The pattern of 1^7 \times 2^7 \times \dots \times 9^7 repeats ten times
solution.description: Note that each range of ten numbers contributes the same set of units digits, so the same block repeats ten times across the expression.

solution.operation: Reduce the problem to the units digit of 1^7 \times 2^7 \times \dots \times 9^7
solution.result: One block of nine factors to evaluate
solution.description: Because the block repeats, check the units digit of a single block of 1^7 through 9^7 instead of the whole expression.

solution.operation: 1^7 \text{ ends in } 1,\; 2^7 \text{ ends in } 8,\; 3^7 \text{ ends in } 7,\; 4^7 \text{ ends in } 4,\; 5^7 \text{ ends in } 5
solution.description: List the units digit of each seventh power in the block, using the cyclicity of each base.
Multiply those units digits together; the block ends in 0, and since the same block repeats for the entire expression, the units digit of the whole product is 0.

key_reminders: The units digit of a product depends only on the units digits of its factors (cyclicity principle).
A repeating block of factors contributes the same units-digit pattern in every range of ten.
common_mistakes: Trying to evaluate the seventh powers themselves instead of tracking only units digits.
Overlooking that the block from 1 to 9 repeats identically for 11-19, 21-29, and so on, and attempting to treat each decade separately.

examples.problem_statement: When x + \frac{1}{x} = 3, find the value of x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2}. Options: 1) 3  2) 6  3) 9  4) 27  5) None of these

solution.description: Square both sides of the given equation so that the squared terms you need appear.
Expand the squared binomial; the cross term 2 \cdot x \cdot (1/x) simplifies to the constant 2.
Subtract the constant cross term from both sides to isolate the requested expression.

key_reminders: For a = x and b = 1/x the cross term 2ab collapses to the constant 2.
common_mistakes: Reporting 9, the square of 3, as the answer without subtracting the cross term.
Squaring termwise as x^2 + 1/x^2 = 9 and forgetting the 2ab middle term entirely.
